There are no known technical challenges that pose a significant threat to the hub being successful in helping the United States meet its emissions-reductions goals. Technically, the hub is fully feasible, being similar to operating terminal hubs in Europe. Entr, who performed most of the preliminary engineering for this study, is heavily involved in successful European hubs. And given its location in an operating industrial port, with nearby terminals already handling potentially dangerous liquefied gases and chemicals, opposition from regulatory bodies or the surrounding community is not anticipated. Page8 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version 2 INTRODUCTION The purpose of this project was to perform a pre-FEED analysis for the design and engineering of the Tampa Regional Intermodal Carbon Hub (“T-RICH”), a comprehensive intermodal transportation hub for captured CO on the west coast of Florida sited at Port Tampa Bay. T-RICH is intended to be the principal 2 gateway for intermediate storage of CO captured from emitters across the State of Florida. The hub will 2 receive, store, process, and load for maritime transport no fewer than 2,000,000 metric tons (mt) of CO 2 per year for permanent sequestration on- and offshore in the Gulf of Mexico region as such underground storage sites receive final Class VI permits. Some of the transported CO could be used for enhanced oil 2 recovery (EOR) in this same region. As a result of the recently passed H.R. 1 bill, EOR now qualifies for the same amount of federal tax credit as for permanent underground sequestration. This project is essential to provide Florida’s largest emitters with a solution for the transport and storage of captured CO . Florida is the third highest emitting state in the U.S. due to the large number of electricity 2 generating power plants that line its Gulf and Atlantic coasts.1 The Tampa Bay region is home to a high concentration of power generating facilities and large industrial CO emitters. Port Tampa Bay has 2 identified a suitable available parcel within the port with access to existing deep-water Berth 30 for the site of the hub. The deep-water berth is critical for the efficient transport of outbound CO on a ship, 2 which will minimize the cost of transport of the CO compared to competing technologies, thereby 2 maximizing project viability.
